title: That is not what you sound like

lines.text: That voice you hear on recordings? That's how everyone else hears you.
When you speak, sound reaches your inner ear in two ways.
Through the air, the same way everyone else hears it.
And through the bones of your head, straight to your inner ear.
Your head boosts the deep, low tones on that second path.
So inside your own head, you sound richer and deeper than you really are.
A recording only captures the air part, so it sounds thinner and higher to you.
But everyone around you has heard that version all along.
So next time you cringe at your voice, remember, that's the real you.

sources.claim: You hear your own voice through air and bone conduction; the head boosts low frequencies, so recordings (air only) sound thinner and higher
